name: MIRACL
listed_description: Multiprecision Integer and Rational Arithmetic Cryptographic
reason: No numeric comparison against a named baseline in any reachable source. The repo README has none, and docs/miracl-explained/benchmarks.md (opened) gives only absolute MIRACL timings (modular exponentiation, RSA, ECDSA, IBE, pairing) on 233 MHz Pentium II, 80 MHz ARM7 and 2.4 GHz Core i5 520 machines with no OpenSSL, GMP, PBC or RELIC column. Third-party shootouts surfaced by search (a search-result snippet of the mcl benchmark table, page not opened: MIRACL ake12bnx 4.2 ms vs mcl 0.31 ms and RELIC 0.30 ms) show MIRACL slower, not faster. Papers said to rank MIRACL ahead of OpenSSL on binary-field curves or of PBC on pairings (Comparative Analysis of Software Libraries for Public Key Cryptography; an SBSeg pairing-library comparison) sit on academia.edu, cryptography.gmu.edu, sol.sbc.org.br and revistas.unisinos.br, all egress blocked, so their numbers could not be checked. Licence is AGPL-3.0 or commercial. Worth a retry from an environment that can open those papers.

name: nanovg
listed_description: Anti-aliased 2D vector drawing library on top of OpenGL, for UI and visualizations
reason: Directional claim only. README says 'small antialiased vector graphics rendering library' with no timings or comparison, and states 'This project is not actively maintained'. iPlug2's wiki page 'IGraphics backend comparison' (opened via raw wiki) calls the NanoVG backend 'Fast (GPU accelerated)' with no numbers. memononen/nanovg issue 113 (opened) names path and stroke tessellation as a bottleneck with no numbers, and the Blend2D issue 3 (opened) asks for comparisons but has none involving NanoVG. The only measured claims found are about forks, not nanovg: styluslabs/nanovgXC claims to be several times faster than Skia on cursory tests (seen only in a search snippet and the repo page title, a separate project). JUCE forum and VCV Rack forum threads that compare NanoVG performance were egress blocked.
